notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-16/17, ~185 queries total. This was an unusually quiet run: search indices appear thin for the exact Oct 16/17 window (multiple lanes reported techmeme/site-specific day queries returning nothing), and the calendar is dense enough that nearly every forward-looking date the lanes re-surfaced (AWS re:Invent, MS Ignite, Google Cloud Next 2027, KubeCon EU 2027, PHP 8.6 GA, PostgreSQL 14/Redis 7.4/Kubernetes 1.35 EOL dates, Apple/Arm earnings, NVIDIA GTC DC, Google Play 16KB deadline) was already on file with equal or better sourcing. The one genuine correction: PostgreSQL 19 now has a real GA target (RC1 shipped, Nov 19 2026 target per postgresql.org itself) replacing a stale September-dated 'expected to release' placeholder that predated any release candidate. The AI lane's one new find, the EU AI Act's Digital Omnibus delay (high-risk Annex III deadline pushed to 2027-12-02, Annex I embedded systems to 2028-08-02, confirmed via Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and corroborated by multiple law-firm summaries), falls outside the 12-month write window from today (2026-10-17) and is recorded here rather than filed, per the far-future-deadline rule — a maintainer re-running this prompt around mid-2027 should pick it up.
concerns: Filed the PostgreSQL 19 GA correction under the title 'PostgreSQL 19 expected general availability after RC1' specifically so its title-token overlap with the existing (now-stale) 'PostgreSQL 19 expected to release' entry clears the isSameThing threshold in src/lib/id.ts and merges instead of creating a second PostgreSQL-19 entry (a title naming the month, e.g. 'November 19', trips isSameThing's month-word same-month-bucket rule and fails to merge across the Oct->Nov date correction, which cost a dry-run iteration to discover). This is the same title-engineering workaround flagged in prior runs' concerns for other entries — a maintainer should loosen or rework that dedupe heuristic so research runs don't need to word titles around it.
